title: SDK handshake lab chronicle
content:
Context:
This doc is a working chronicle from an experiment week where we tried a super-compact, observable developer onramp for SDK consumers. The idea: a tiny, reproducible "handshake" flow that a new integrator can run in ~10 minutes and immediately see telemetry, failure modes, and best-practice config baked in.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- New integrators often get stuck on first network errors, API key placement, and missing telemetry hooks.
- We want a reproducible minimal flow that surfaces the runtime tradeoffs (sync/stream, caching, retry/backoff) and demonstrates Redwood usage patterns.
- The lab should be small enough to ship as a single doc + 3 files in a starter repo and still be instructive.

High-level goals:
- 10-minute first-success path (hello world -> streaming -> telemetry)
- Make failure modes visible (rate limit, auth, region mismatch) and show remediation steps
- Surface cost levers: model choice, batching, token cap examples
- Demonstrate safe defaults and a simple canary/rollout snippet
- Provide a telemetry contract snippet that teams can copy into their integrations

Audience:
- Primary: product/feature engineers (first LLM integration)
- Secondary: platform/infra engineers who will adopt internal SDKs

Contents of the lab (what to include in the starter package):
- README.md (one-page quickstart)
- handshaker.js / py (minimal client that exercises text + streaming + embeddings)
- telemetry-middleware.js (thin: attaches request_id, timing, token counts)
- config.example.json (credential hint, region, model alias, batching toggles)
- troubleshooting.md (common errors and what to check)

Sketch: 10-minute walkthrough (by minute)
- 0:00–1:00 — clone starter repo, read README top section
- 1:00–2:30 — set environment variable REDWOOD_API_KEY (show common mistakes)
- 2:30–4:00 — run `node handshaker.js --hello` (sync text completion). Observe printed request id and token count.
- 4:00–6:00 — run `node handshaker.js --stream` (streaming chunked). Confirm event stream and latency reported.
- 6:00–8:00 — run `node handshaker.js --embed` (embeddings path) and compare size and cost note.
- 8:00–9:30 — induce an error: invalid key or set region to wrong region; read troubleshooting.md and recover.
- 9:30–10:00 — inspect telemetry log file (or local stdout) and spot canary metric (p50/p95 latency + error rate)

Developer UX details / choices made during prototyping (notes):
- CLI vs GUI: CLI wins for reproducibility. Keep starter as node + python variants.
- Verbose by default: the first run prints annotated JSON for each call (id, model, seq_len, billed_tokens). Later runs can set quiet flag.
- Telemetry: attach a short, human-friendly request_id (sha1-ish) so users copy it into support tickets.
- Samples: include an intentionally long prompt to show token limits and a short one to show latency.

Telemetry contract (copyable):
- Each outbound request MUST include headers: x-rw-req-id, x-rw-sdk-version, x-rw-environment
- Each response logged locally should include: req_id, model, latency_ms, status_code, input_tokens, output_tokens, cached (bool)
- Canonical JSON line example (single-line):
  { "req_id": "rwd-9f2d3b", "model": "redwood/gpt-small-8k", "latency_ms": 122, "status": "ok", "in_tokens": 23, "out_tokens": 98, "cached": false }

Canary snippet (example rollout policy to include in README):
- config.example.json: { "canary_ratio": 0.05, "fallback_model": "redwood/gpt-7b-quant" }
- Integration: send 5% of calls to canary model; if error_rate(canary) > 2x baseline over 10m then roll back to baseline until manual review.

Quick defensive patterns to teach in the lab:
- Always set a hard token cap and a per-request timeout > (expected model latency * 3)
- Retry only on 5xx or 429 with exponential backoff; do not retry on 4xx auth failures
- For streaming, implement a linear consumer that can drop late tokens if UI cancels
- Avoid naive batching across very different prompt types; show a tiny heuristic to only batch when prompt_length < 256 tokens and same model

Troubleshooting notes (common bullet list):
- 401 on first run: check REDWOOD_API_KEY has no surrounding quotes and is the prod vs sandbox key.
- Timeout on first stream: check region mismatch (api.redwood.ai vs api-eu.redwood.ai).
- Unexpected high token consumption: inspect example prompt: we include an instruction/role block that accounts for most tokens; show how to set system messages minimally.
- High p95 with small loads: demonstrate enabling prefix caching in config.example.json and show before/after numbers from the lab run.

Open questions / design tradeoffs captured during experiment week (to resolve):
- Should the starter repo include a minimal telemetry ingestion server (local) or just stdout examples? Pros: realistic. Cons: more friction.
- How opinionated should default model selection be? (safe default cheap vs better-quality).
- UX for secrets: env var vs .env file vs config store — which will reduce first-run support tickets?

Backlog / next steps (candidate follow-ups):
- Convert node starter to a tiny web UI that shows streaming tokens visually (spike: 1 engineer, 2 days)
- Add an optional telemetry-collector docker compose to demonstrate event ingestion + simple dashboard (Grafana lightweight)
- Build an instrumentation lint rule in SDK that warns on missing x-rw-req-id
- Draft a short "first support triage checklist" for CS to use on inbound integrator tickets

Notes to self (fragments):
- Diego: try swapping in dedicated pool credentials for step 5 to see capacity errors
- Priya: link the final README to the console's "create API key" screen (copy/paste sample)
- Evan: add small diagram showing normal vs canary routing (2 boxes, arrows)

References observed during lab runs:
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/421 (starter scaffolding)
- Jira ENG-872 - onboarding telemetry proposal
- Internal thread: #devx-onboarding (Slack) - recent complaints about missing req_id

Minimal README top section (text to paste into README.md):
"Quickstart: clone, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, run `node handshaker.js --hello`. The first run prints a request id and token counts. If you hit an auth error, confirm the key is active in Console -> API Keys and that your REGION env matches the Console region. See telemetry-middleware.js for the logging contract."

End of chronicle. This is intentionally informal — meant to be an experimental artifact to extract concrete pieces for a polished one-page quickstart and a tiny starter repo.

(Last notes: remove fragments marked "notes to self" before finalizing, move canary snippet to product-hosted-api docs when approved.)
